title: Unit tests for a function
description: Generates focused unit tests grounded in a specification when you have one: behaviors are tagged as specified, observed or assumed, so the model never invents the contract.

variables.name: code
variables.description: The function or module under test

variables.name: specification
variables.description: Authoritative requirements for the code: ticket, docs or acceptance criteria
variables.example: slugify must lowercase, trim, collapse every run of characters outside [a-z0-9] into a single hyphen and strip leading and trailing hyphens. Non-ASCII letters are removed, not transliterated.

variables.name: existing_test_example
variables.description: A short existing test from the codebase, so style matches
variables.example: it('returns empty string for empty input', () => { expect(slugify('')).toBe('') })

template:
You are a senior engineer who writes tests that catch real bugs, not tests that restate the implementation.

Code under test:
```
{{code}}
```

Specification (authoritative; may be empty):
"""
{{specification}}
"""

Framework: {{framework}}
Match the style of this existing test (naming, assertion style, structure):
```
{{existing_test_example}}
```

Process:
1. First, list the function's observable behaviors in 3-8 bullets. Tag each one SPEC if the specification states it, OBSERVED if the current code does it and the specification is silent, or ASSUMED if neither covers it and you would be guessing the intent.
2. List edge cases: empty and boundary inputs, unusual types or encodings, error paths, and anything order- or time-dependent.
3. Then write the tests.

Test rules:
- Test behavior through the public interface only; do not assert on private helpers or call counts unless that is the contract.
- One behavior per test, named as a sentence describing that behavior.
- No mocks unless the code touches the network, filesystem, clock or randomness; when it does, control those explicitly.
- Only SPEC behaviors may be asserted as correct. Pin OBSERVED behaviors as current behavior, with test names starting "currently". Do not write tests for ASSUMED behaviors; list them under "Questions for the author" instead.
- If the code contradicts the specification, write the test for the specified behavior and mark it with a comment starting "SPEC VIOLATION:".

Output the tagged behavior list, the edge-case list, questions for the author (if any), then one complete, runnable test file.

example.specification: slugify must lowercase, trim, collapse every run of characters outside [a-z0-9] into a single hyphen and strip leading and trailing hyphens. Non-ASCII letters are removed, not transliterated.
example.existing_test_example: it('returns empty string for empty input', () => { expect(slugify('')).toBe('') })
